title: Construct bilayer structural models
action: Obtain the bulk crystal structure of Ca3Ru2O7 from Yoshida et al. (2005). Using the provided surface atomic displacements (octahedral rotation angle, tilt angle, vertical shifts of Ca, O, Ru atoms), create two free-standing bilayer models: a bulk-like bilayer (using bulk atomic positions) and a surface-relaxed bilayer (with the displacements applied). Include a vacuum gap of about 15 Å between periodic images. Set up the initial magnetic order as AFM_b (spins along the b-axis). Output the two structural models (e.g., in CIF or POSCAR format) as evidence that the geometry preparation was performed.
description: Prepare the input geometries required for the DFT calculations. The surface displacements (rotation ≈13°, tilt ≈13°, vertical shifts for Ca, O, Ru atoms) are provided in the task description and correspond to the experimentally determined surface relaxation. No symmetry-breaking reconstruction is applied.

title: Run DFT+U sweeps and extract band gaps
action: For each of the two bilayer geometries (bulk-like and surface-relaxed) and each Hubbard U value in {0.0, 2.5, 2.625, 2.75} eV, perform a self-consistent DFT+U calculation using the LDA functional, spin-orbit coupling, and AFM_b magnetic order. Apply the U parameter to Ru 4d states within the Dudarev approximation. Use a suitable k-point grid and plane-wave energy cutoff to converge the band gap. After convergence, compute the total density of states (DOS) and determine the band gap at the Fermi level. If a gap exists (e.g., DOS at Ef below 0.01 eV), set band_gap_eV > 0 and is_insulator=true; otherwise set band_gap_eV ≈ 0 and is_insulator=false. Write all results into /app/outputs/step_01_band_gaps.json as an object with a 'calculations' array containing objects with keys geometry, U_eV, band_gap_eV, is_insulator.
description: The main computational reproduction: the U-dependent metal-insulator transition. The output lists the band gap and insulating flag for each calculation, enabling verification of the surface-only insulating window.
